author: The Infographics Show
description:
Tokyo is one of the most important cities on Earth, and Japan knows a massive earthquake could cripple it almost overnight. That’s why the country is preparing a backup plan designed to keep the government, financial system, and economy alive if the capital goes down.

This video explores Japan’s emerging “doomsday protocol,” including plans for a second capital, most likely Osaka, that could take over critical government functions after a catastrophic Nankai Trough earthquake. We examine the enormous economic risk concentrated in Tokyo, from banking and government operations to semiconductor supply chains that the entire world depends on.
Japan is also building redundant infrastructure, including backup Bank of Japan systems and a future Maglev connection between Tokyo and Osaka. But major weaknesses remain. Political resistance, delayed construction, outdated paper-based administration, and no fully tested plan for relocating national leadership during a disaster.
